verdict.waiting: Waiting for data from the core
verdict.waitingHint: The daemon stream has just opened: the numbers will appear in a couple of seconds.
verdict.startingHint: The core is starting: numbers will appear in a few seconds.
verdict.offlineHint: The numbers below are not updating. The panel reconnects on its own; if it does not, check that the router is reachable over the network.
verdict.silentHint: The daemon responds, but the core is sending no data. Check the log for the cause.
verdict.stoppedHint: Traffic does not pass through the core. Start it with the Start button in the Core card below. Check the log for the cause.
verdict.nodeDown: The selected node does not respond
verdict.nodeDownHint: Traffic through this node does not get through. Pick another node or test the latency again.
verdict.hotHint: From {{limit}} °C the board lowers its clock. Check the cooling and the load in the Router section below.
verdict.warmHint: There is headroom before {{limit}} °C, where the board lowers its clock. The temperature is in the Router section below.
verdict.foreign: The core is running outside metabox
verdict.foreignHint: Another service started the core and manages its commands.
verdict.okHint: The routing core is running and data is coming in.

node.title: Node
node.noGroups: The config has no groups: rules send traffic straight to outbounds.
node.none: No group has manual choice: the other groups pick their node themselves. Add one on the Proxies screen.

check.title: Quick check
check.hint: Sends packets from the router and records the check in the core log.
check.label: Check results

traffic.title: Where traffic went
traffic.internetHelp: An internet connection is how the router reaches the internet. A router can have several, for example one for the main provider and one for a backup.
traffic.directHelp: Direct includes traffic sent directly by rules and an estimated {{volume}} that bypassed the core. A direct outbound shows only the traffic the core sent through that outbound.
traffic.waiting: Waiting for the first traffic snapshot
traffic.history: The core is stopped. New core traffic readings will appear after it starts.

blocked.label: Blocked connections
blocked.unavailableLabel: Why the blocked count is unavailable
blocked.computedHelp: Counts blocked connections recorded in the core log since the daemon started.
blocked.incomplete: Some earlier log lines are missing. The count stays unavailable until the daemon restarts.
blocked.levelHelp: In the log section of the config, enable logging and set log.level to debug for reject rules or info for a block outbound. If you use both, choose debug. It writes several lines per connection. Apply the config to use the new level.
